access-rules.help: Manage IP Access rules (whitelist, block, challenge)
access-rules.usage_instructions: Use `cloudflare access-rules` for manage ip access rules (whitelist, block, challenge). Available subcommands here are `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `delete`.

create.help: Create a new IP Access rule.
examples: cloudflare access-rules create ZONE_ID --target ip --value 1.2.3.4 --mode whitelist
cloudflare access-rules create ZONE_ID --target ip_range --value 10.0.0.0/8 --mode whitelist --notes "Internal network"
cloudflare access-rules create ZONE_ID --target asn --value AS12345 --mode block
cloudflare access-rules create ZONE_ID --target country --value CN --mode challenge
create.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare access-rules create` to create a new IP Access rule. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`. Common options: `--table`.

options.name: --target
options.help: Target type (ip, ip_range, asn, country, ipv6)

options.name: --value
options.help: Target value (IP, CIDR, ASN, country code)

options.name: --mode
options.help: Action mode (whitelist, block, challenge, js_challenge, managed_challenge)

delete.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare access-rules delete` to delete an IP Access rule. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`, `RULE_ID`. Common options: `--force/-f`.

get.help: Get details for a specific IP Access rule.
get.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare access-rules get` to get details for a specific IP Access rule. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`, `RULE_ID`. Common options: `--table/-t`.

list.help: List IP Access rules for a zone.
list.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare access-rules list` to list IP Access rules for a zone. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`. Common options: `--table/-t`, `--limit/-l`, `--filter/-f`, `--properties/-p`.

options.name: --limit
options.help: Maximum number of rules to return (max 50)

examples: cloudflare access-rules update ZONE_ID RULE_ID --mode challenge
cloudflare access-rules update ZONE_ID RULE_ID --notes "Updated description"
cloudflare access-rules update ZONE_ID RULE_ID --mode block --notes "Banned"
update.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare access-rules update` to update an IP Access rule. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`, `RULE_ID`. Options: `--mode/-m`, `--notes/-n`.

summary.help: Show zone traffic totals for a date range. Totals come from the httpRequests1dGroups daily rollup dataset: page views, unique visitors, requests, and bytes. unique_visitors is the sum of per-day uniques, not deduplicated across days.

arguments.name: zone
arguments.help: Zone name (e.g. example.com) or 32-character zone ID

options.name: --start
options.help: Start date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive (default: 30 days ago)

top-paths.help: Show top request paths by HTML page views for a date range. Uses the httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups dataset filtered to edge responses with content type "html" (page views). Data is adaptively sampled by Cloudflare, and pct_of_total is each path's share of all HTML page views in the range. Dataset retention varies by plan, so old ranges may return no data.

arguments.name: zone
arguments.help: Zone name (e.g. example.com) or 32-character zone ID

options.name: --start
options.help: Start date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive (default: 30 days ago)

options.name: --limit
options.help: Maximum number of paths to return

auth.usage_instructions: Use `cloudflare auth` for manage authentication. Available subcommands here are `login`, `logout`, `status`, `test`, `profiles`.

login.help: Configure authentication credentials. Prompts for required credentials based on the tool's authentication type. For OAuth authorization code flows, opens a browser for user consent.

options.name: --profile
options.help: Profile name to save credentials to

options.name: --force
options.help: Clear existing ephemeral auth state and re-authenticate

logout.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare auth logout` to clear stored credentials. Common options: `--profile/-p`.

options.name: --profile
options.help: Profile name to clear credentials from

profiles.usage_instructions: Use `cloudflare auth profiles` for manage authentication profiles. Available subcommands here are `list`, `get`, `create`, `set-default`, `delete`.

create.help: Create a new profile from .env.example template.
create.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare auth profiles create` to create a new profile from .env.example template. Required arguments: `NAME`.

delete.help: Delete a profile and its data.
delete.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare auth profiles delete` to delete a profile and its data. Required arguments: `NAME`. Common options: `--force/-F`.

get.help: Get details for a specific profile.
get.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare auth profiles get` to get details for a specific profile. Required arguments: `NAME`. Common options: `--table/-t`.

list.help: List all profiles and show auth type and active state.
list.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare auth profiles list` to list all profiles and show which is the default. Common options: `--table/-t`, `--limit/-l`, `--filter/-f`, `--properties/-p`.

options.name: --limit
options.help: Maximum number of profiles to return

select.help: Activate a profile within its auth type.

arguments.name: name
arguments.help: Profile name to activate within its auth type

status.help: Check authentication status across profiles. Performs a live round-trip for every configured credential type so the report reflects ground truth — not on-disk belief. Saved credentials whose live verification fails are reported as ``authenticated: false`` with the failure reason in ``api_test``.
status.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare auth status` to check authentication status across profiles. Performs a live round-trip for every configured credential type so the report reflects ground truth — not on-disk belief. Saved credentials whose live verification fails are reported as ``authenticated: false`` with the failure reason in ``api_test``. Common options: `--table/-t`, `--profile/-p`.

options.name: --profile
options.help: Profile name to check (defaults to all profiles)

test.help: Test authentication by verifying credentials work across profiles.
test.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare auth test` to test authentication by verifying credentials work across profiles. Common options: `--table/-t`, `--profile/-p`.

cache.usage_instructions: Use `cloudflare cache` for manage cloudflare cache. Available subcommands here are `purge`.

clear.help: Remove all cached responses. Deletes every file in the cache directory ({storage_dir}/cache/) and reports how many files and bytes were freed.

purge.help: Purge all cache for a zone. WARNING: This will purge ALL cached content for the zone.
purge.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare cache purge` to purge all cache for a zone. WARNING: This will purge ALL cached content for the zone. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`. Common options: `--table/-t`, `--force/-F`.

arguments.name: zone_id
arguments.help: The zone ID to purge cache for

dns.usage_instructions: Use `cloudflare dns` for manage dns records. Available subcommands here are `zones`, `records`.

records.usage_instructions: Use `cloudflare dns records` for manage dns records. Available subcommands here are `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `delete`.

examples: cloudflare dns records create ZONE_ID --type A --name example.com --content 1.2.3.4
cloudflare dns records create ZONE_ID --type A --name example.com --content 1.2.3.4 --proxied
cloudflare dns records create ZONE_ID --type CNAME --name www.example.com --content example.com
cloudflare dns records create ZONE_ID --type TXT --name example.com --content "v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all"
cloudflare dns records create ZONE_ID --type MX --name example.com --content mail.example.com --priority 10
create.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare dns records create` to create a new DNS record. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`. Common options: `--table/-t`.

options.name: --type
options.help: Record type (A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, MX, etc.)

options.name: --ttl
options.help: TTL in seconds (1 = auto, 60-86400 for custom)

examples: cloudflare dns records delete ZONE_ID RECORD_ID
cloudflare dns records delete ZONE_ID RECORD_ID --force
delete.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare dns records delete` to delete a DNS record. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`, `RECORD_ID`. Common options: `--force/-f`.

get.help: Get details for a specific DNS record.
examples: cloudflare dns records get ZONE_ID RECORD_ID
cloudflare dns records get ZONE_ID RECORD_ID --table
get.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare dns records get` to get details for a specific DNS record. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`, `RECORD_ID`. Common options: `--table/-t`.

list.help: List DNS records for a zone.
examples: cloudflare dns records list ZONE_ID --type TXT
list.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare dns records list` to list DNS records for a zone. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`. Common options: `--table/-t`, `--limit/-l`, `--filter/-f`, `--properties`.

options.name: --limit
options.help: Maximum number of records to return (max 5000)

examples: cloudflare dns records update ZONE_ID RECORD_ID --content 5.6.7.8
cloudflare dns records update ZONE_ID RECORD_ID --proxied true
cloudflare dns records update ZONE_ID RECORD_ID --ttl 3600 --comment "Updated"
update.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare dns records update` to update a DNS record. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`, `RECORD_ID`. Options: `--type/-T`, `--name/-n`, `--content/-c`, `--ttl`, `--proxied/-p`, `--priority`.

zones.usage_instructions: Use `cloudflare dns zones` for list and inspect dns zones. Available subcommands here are `list`, `get`.

get.help: Get details for a specific DNS zone.
get.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare dns zones get` to get details for a specific DNS zone. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`. Common options: `--table/-t`.

list.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare dns zones list` to list DNS zones. Common options: `--table/-t`, `--limit/-l`, `--filter/-f`, `--properties/-p`.

options.name: --limit
options.help: Maximum number of zones to return (max 50)

arguments.name: account
arguments.help: Account name or ID (defaults to the single visible account)

get.help: Download a Worker script's source content.
examples: cloudflare workers get my-worker my-account --output worker.js

arguments.name: account
arguments.help: Account name or ID (defaults to the single visible account)

options.name: --output
options.help: Write the script content to this file instead of stdout

list.help: List Workers scripts for an account.

arguments.name: account
arguments.help: Account name or ID (defaults to the single visible account)

options.name: --limit
options.help: Maximum number of scripts to return

upload.help: Upload (create or replace) a Worker script.

arguments.name: account
arguments.help: Account name or ID (defaults to the single visible account)

options.name: --file
options.help: Path to the script source ('-' for stdin)

zones.usage_instructions: Use `cloudflare zones` for manage cloudflare zones. Available subcommands here are `list`, `get`, `update`.

get.help: Get details for a specific zone.
get.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare zones get` to get details for a specific zone. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`. Common options: `--table/-t`, `--properties/-p`.

list.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare zones list` to list Cloudflare zones. Common options: `--table/-t`, `--limit/-l`, `--filter/-f`, `--properties/-p`.

options.name: --limit
options.help: Maximum number of zones to return (max 50)

update.usage_instructions: Run `cloudflare zones update` to update zone settings. Required arguments: `ZONE_ID`. Options: `--security-level/-s`.

options.name: --security-level
options.help: Set security level (off, essentially_off, low, medium, high, under_attack)

usage_instructions: Use for cli interface for cloudflare api. Commands follow `cloudflare <group> <action>`. Primary groups here are `cloudflare auth`, `cloudflare zones`, `cloudflare cache`, `cloudflare access-rules`, `cloudflare dns`.
